display.title: Episode 524: The Cup of Eliyahu HaNavi (Yud-Aleph Nissan)
display.summary_short: On the Rebbe's 90th birthday, just before Pesach, Uncle Yossi speaks about unity in Tzivos Hashem, a five-year-old says the Shema, and a poor woman who refuses to sell her Kos shel Eliyahu is rewarded.
display.summary_long: Broadcast on Yud-Aleph Nissan 5752, the Rebbe's 90th birthday, days before Pesach. Uncle Yossi explains the Rebbe's teaching that Tzivos Hashem unites tens of thousands of children in good deeds, and that unity, 'bless us, our Father, all of us as one', is the secret of the Jewish people's strength. Even a newborn can be enrolled, and children who were first to recognize Hashem at the Exodus will be first to greet Moshiach, so listeners are urged to sign up friends before Pesach. After a prayer for the Rebbe's recovery and the Hakochainik march, a five-year-old yeshiva boy recites the Shema, and everyone gives tzedakah. Uncle Yossi explains Eliyahu HaNavi's role as herald of Moshiach and his visit to every Seder, then tells the story: Devorah treasures a jeweled golden Kos shel Eliyahu passed down in her family. Her husband, too poor to prepare for Pesach, wants to sell it, but she refuses. She shelters an old beggar from a rainstorm, and the gold coin he gives her keeps returning to her table. At the Seder he reveals himself as Eliyahu HaNavi. The show closes with birthday wishes for the Rebbe and a wish for a kosher and happy Pesach.
display.lesson: Honor the mitzvos even when it is hard, trust in Hashem, and be kind to every guest; Hashem's help can come in surprising ways.
